review_reference: Decision relayed by the user in chat on 2026-11-11, answering which rule Outreach campaign management should follow (ADR-045's open question): "Campaign admins only (Recommended)", option B. Any staff member allowed to write campaigns may create one and becomes its admin; only that campaign's own admins open or close it and add members, enforced in outreach-api and in the database. Numbered 0122 when written; 0122 is now taken by #223 (sign-up fields), so it takes the next free number when it merges (the owner names it). reviewed_by is empty until the owner signs this declaration.
evidence: Single migration 0122_outreach_campaign_admins.sql, unsigned until the owner signs (reviewed_by is empty). WHAT IT DOES: (1) CREATE OR REPLACE of outreach.validate_campaign_write() (0077's body, md5 1ac1e424e645378ab6e88a45542fccf9, kept whole) adding, on UPDATE, that the session's membership is an admin member of the campaign, else 42501 'Outreach campaign admin is required'; owner, SECURITY DEFINER and search_path unchanged; a row lock fires no trigger, so 0045's FOR SHARE on registration is unaffected. (2) Two RESTRICTIVE policies on outreach.campaign_members: insert only by an admin member of the campaign, or by its creator seeding themself as the first admin of a campaign with no member; delete only by an admin member. 0038's permissive policies stay. (3) outreach.campaign_staff(uuid) RETURNS TABLE(membership_id uuid, display_name text, campaign_role text), plpgsql, STABLE, SECURITY DEFINER, search_path pg_catalog, platform, auth, identity, outreach, owned by outreach.campaigns' owner, EXECUTE for hid_outreach_runtime only: to a member of the campaign holding outreach.campaign.read at the session facility, its members (identity.staff.full_name and campaign role); to its admins also every active staff membership at the facility (campaign role null); anyone else no row; at most 1000 rows. No table, column, constraint, index, role or other function changes; no row read or written. BACKWARD COMPATIBLE: today's identity-api refuses outreach.campaign.write, so no API path reaches a campaign write; campaign reads and registrations are unchanged. RELEASE ORDER: the owner signs this; apply 0122; release outreach-api; release identity-api last (it is what accepts outreach.campaign.write). FILES: the migration and services/ehr-api/database/runtime-grants.sql, which gains 0122's two lines (revoke outreach.campaign_staff(uuid) from public; grant EXECUTE to hid_outreach_runtime), as the release requires every changed file under services/ehr-api/database/ to be declared (#224). BASELINE: written on 0001-0108 and brought up to staging 13d5b518 (0109 and 0110 live); 0110 replaces the registration trigger's body (validate_registration_campaign_write), not the campaign trigger replaced here, and changes no policy, grant or RLS setting that 0122 pins. PRECONDITIONS (catalog reads only; 55000 or 42501, nothing applied): 0001-0110 applied (0110's outreach.validate_registration_campaign_write() body md5 69469315f04554d2639dfa9f83591d4d, the marker); not applied yet; the trigger function's body and attributes as 0077 left them and its trigger present; FORCE RLS on both campaign tables with 0038's policies; identity.staff and staff_facility_memberships not FORCE RLS; the applier may SET ROLE to the owner, which owns the trigger function and has CREATE on schema outreach. POST-CHECKS: the trigger function's attributes and owner, the two restrictive policies, campaign_staff's attributes, result and ACL. PROVED on local PostgreSQL 16.15 clusters (created and deleted): every SQL suite on a fresh install of 0001-0110 and 0122; the upgrade rehearsal services/ehr-api/scripts/test-staging-schema-upgrade.mjs (HID_REHEARSAL_ADMIN_URL, a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS migrator, baseline 0001-0110, declared exactly 0122); and the new suite and outreach-session-guards on a database whose migrator is NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS. SUITE: services/ehr-api/test/database/outreach-campaign-admins.integration.sql, 24 cases as hid_outreach_api_runtime: an admin opens and closes, an enumerator, a non-member, an admin of another campaign and the creator who is no longer an admin are refused, another clinic changes nothing; a member's FOR SHARE lock still succeeds; an admin adds members and a second admin, an enumerator and a non-member cannot (themselves included), the creator cannot seed into a campaign with members, a creator seeds themself and nobody else; an enumerator removes no member and an admin can; campaign_staff to an admin, a member, a non-member, another clinic and an unknown campaign; the EHR runtime cannot call it. outreach-session-guards.integration.sql: its fixture campaign's creator is seeded as its admin (as createCampaign does) and campaign updates by another membership, or none, now expect the admin refusal; where the trigger's owner does not bypass RLS, A's sessions without direct care are refused as not an admin as well, since the check reads the members under their policies (121 cases in both shapes).
